record.summary: A 20-acre active Caltrain rail yard and maintenance facility at the nexus of SoMa, Mission Bay and Showplace Square, including the existing 4th & King Street Station itself. Owned by Prologis, with Caltrain holding a perpetual easement to operate rail. SF Planning is processing it as the "SF Railyards Planning Program" (Case No. 2023-000384CWP); Prologis has floated a development concept of up to 2,500 housing units and about 8 million square feet in total (about half commercial), anchored by a tower as tall as 850 feet (SF Standard, March 2026); a Development Agreement is the expected approval path, the same one used for Pier 70, Mission Rock and Potrero Power Station.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- not a surveyed parcel or a GIS file from Caltrain/Prologis/SF Planning. Correction (2026-09-29): this polygon is not free of Assessor parcels. DataSF's Parcels - Active and Retired dataset (as of 2026-05-31) carries three active secured-roll parcels lying wholly inside it (8701004, 700 4th St; 8701003, 311 Townsend St; 8700001, 797 7th St; together about 82% of its area), so the earlier statement that the rail right-of-way carries no block/lot was wrong. It stays an approximate feature here; whether it should instead be mapped as real parcels has not yet been decided. Three of the four sides (Townsend, 4th, 7th) are real, continuous DataSF street centerlines; the fourth (King St plus a straight closing line at the I-280 interchange, drawn on the earlier belief that King's DataSF centerline ended short of 7th; see the correction to how this shape was traced) is the weakest edge and the one most likely to need revision if a real project boundary or EIR figure becomes available. Includes the existing Caltrain 4th & King Street Station itself, which the project's own description treats as part of the site being redeveloped, not something outside it.
notes.digitized_from: Bounded by DataSF's official street centerlines: Townsend St (4th-7th) on the north, 4th St (Townsend-King) on the east, 7th St (Townsend-King) on the west, and King St (4th-~6th) on the south, each widened by the standard measured half-width used across this map (6.8m) and inset from the outer street-to-street ring by that same half-width to approximate the curb/yard edge rather than the street centerline itself -- the same method as P9. Correction (2026-09-29): the earlier text here said King St's DataSF centerline stops short of 7th St. It does not: the dataset has King St segments from 6th to 7th St (06TH ST -> 07TH ST, (-122.398585, 37.77289) to (-122.400804, 37.771138), plus '06TH ST - END: WEST' and 'END: EAST - 07TH ST' pieces); only the 5th-6th St segment ends at (-122.397986, 37.773324), and the next segment begins about 70 m further on. I-280 ramp segments are in the dataset too. The southern closing edge was drawn as a straight line from that 5th-6th point to 7th St's King-St corner and has not been re-checked against the 6th-7th St King segments (the geometry is unchanged). The resulting inset polygon is 20.08 acres, matching the SF Planning/Caltrain FAQ's own '20-acre site' description almost exactly, and its outline was checked directly against an overlay on Esri World Imagery -- it tracks the real fan of tracks and the 4th & King station platform canopy tightly, confirmed by Pier & Point on 2026-09-21 after a side-by-side review of the overlay.

changes.text: New adjacent record: the SF Railyards, a 20-acre active Caltrain rail yard and the 4th & King Street Station, owned by Prologis with Caltrain holding a perpetual operating easement, adjoining Mission Bay North. SF Planning is processing it as the "SF Railyards Planning Program" (Case No. 2023-000384CWP, per the January 2025 Planning Commission packet); Prologis has floated a concept of up to 2,500 housing units and about 8 million square feet in total (about half commercial), with an 850-foot tower (SF Standard, March 10, 2026); a Development Agreement is the expected approval path (SF Planning FAQ). The map shape is bounded by real street centerlines (Townsend, 4th, 7th, King), not a surveyed parcel; see the record's accuracy note. Pier & Point records the process and does not take a position.

open_questions: Whether Prologis's March 2026 submission constitutes a formal Preliminary Project Assessment/application distinct from the January 2025 informational Case No. 2023-000384CWP, or is still pre-application, is not confirmed here -- SF Planning's project page and hearing calendar are the places to check.

No named individual or group's public position on this specific project (for or against) has been found and sourced yet, distinct from the SF Railyards Working Group's general, collectively-summarized 'conceptual support' described in the January 2025 staff report.

The site's geometry is bounded by real street centerlines on three sides; the fourth (where King St's real centerline data ends short of 7th St, at the I-280 interchange) is a straight closing line, not a surveyed street -- see the shape's accuracy caveat.

As of 2026-09-29: the SF Chronicle article (January 8, 2025) reports the 850-foot tower concept but says it is too early to say how many units; the 2,500-unit and 8-million-sq-ft figures come from the SF Standard (March 10, 2026). The project page does not itself state the Development Agreement path, the FAQ does. Three active Assessor parcels lie inside this site's polygon (see the shape's accuracy caveat); whether this should be a real-parcel record is unresolved.

record.notes: SF Planning Case No. 2023-000384CWP, 'SF Railyards Planning Program'. The 20-acre site at the nexus of SoMa, Mission Bay and Showplace Square: Caltrain's northern terminus and an active service/maintenance yard, owned by Prologis with Caltrain holding a perpetual easement to operate rail. A Development Agreement is the expected approval path (precedent: Pier 70, Mission Rock, Potrero Power Station, all DAs). Adjoins Mission Bay North. OCII's December 2019 Mission Bay Land Use Map, as seen in the map image (linked in this record's sources), labels N5A, N6 and N7 in this area with no land-use color and no drawn boundary, unlike the numbered Mission Bay North blocks beside it. That does not settle whether the site lies outside Mission Bay North: in DataSF's redevelopment project areas layer about 41% of this polygon lies inside 'Mission Bay - North', and parcels 8701003 and 8701004 are zoned MB-O. The map PDF and the project-area boundary have not yet been checked to settle this.
